## Welcome to the Lab!

Today you'll analyse the data **you** collected in the Foundations Datalab session.

**Time**: ~90 minutes

**Structure**:

1. **Setup** (10 min) - Load data, find yourself
2. **Activity 1** (25 min) - Describe & Visualise
3. **Activity 2** (25 min) - Test a Hypothesis
4. **Activity 3** (25 min) - Explore a Relationship
5. **Wrap-up** (15 min) - Share findings

::: {.callout-note}
## Deliverables
By the end, you should have:

- 1 histogram with interpretation
- 1 statistical test with interpretation
- 1 scatterplot with correlation
:::

---

# Setup {#setup}

## Load the Data


## Variable Guide

Here's what each variable means:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `participant_id` | Your ID (e.g., A01, B05) |
| `lab_room` | 1 = Lab A (silence), 2 = Lab B (music) |
| `mood_pre_1` / `mood_post_1` | Mood rating (1-10) |
| `energy_pre_1` / `energy_post_1` | Energy rating (1-10) |
| `stress_pre_1` / `stress_post_1` | Stress rating (1-10) |
| `mem_total_1` | Words recalled (out of 10) |
| `time_estimate_sec` | Time estimate (seconds) |
| `throw_self_rating_1` | Self-rated throwing ability |
| `throw_dom_success` | Dominant hand hits (out of 10) |
| `throw_nondom_success` | Non-dominant hand hits (out of 5) |
| `rt_mean` | Mean reaction time (ms) |
| `stare_accuracy` | Sixth sense accuracy (0-1) |
| `tipi_1` | Extraversion score |

## Find Yourself!

Enter your participant ID to find your row:

```{webr-r}
# Change this to YOUR participant ID
my_id <- "B01"

# Find your data
my_data <- merged |> filter(participant_id == my_id)
my_data
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Where Are You?
Run this to see where you fall on the mood distribution:
```{webr-r}
ggplot(merged, aes(x = mood_pre_1)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "grey70", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = my_data$mood_pre_1,
             color = "red", linewidth = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = my_data$mood_pre_1 + 0.3, y = 3,
           label = "YOU", color = "red", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(x = "Pre-Session Mood", y = "Count", title = "Where Are You?")
```
:::

# Activity 1: Describe & Visualise {#activity1}

**Time**: 25 minutes

**Goal**: Create a histogram and describe a distribution

## Step 1: Choose a Variable

Pick ONE continuous variable to explore:

- `mood_pre_1` - Starting mood
- `time_estimate_sec` - Time estimation
- `rt_mean` - Reaction time
- `mem_total_1` - Memory performance

```{webr-r}
# Choose your variable
my_variable <- "rt_mean"  # Change this!

# Pull out just that column
my_values <- merged |> pull(!!sym(my_variable))
```

## Step 2: Calculate Descriptive Statistics

```{webr-r}
# Calculate statistics
tibble(
  Statistic = c("N", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Max", "Median"),
  Value = c(
    length(my_values),
    round(mean(my_values, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    round(sd(my_values, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    min(my_values, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(my_values, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(my_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
```

## Step 3: Create a Histogram

```{webr-r}
# Create your histogram
ggplot(merged, aes(x = .data[[my_variable]])) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = "#3498db", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(my_values, na.rm = TRUE),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = my_variable,
    y = "Count",
    title = paste("Distribution of", my_variable),
    subtitle = "Red line = mean"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## Step 4: Assess Normality

Is your distribution approximately normal?

```{webr-r}
# Skewness (rough assessment)
# If mean ≈ median, likely symmetric
cat("Mean:", round(mean(my_values, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
cat("Median:", median(my_values, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("\nIf mean > median: positive skew (tail to right)")
cat("\nIf mean < median: negative skew (tail to left)")
cat("\nIf mean ≈ median: approximately symmetric")
```

# Activity 2: Test a Hypothesis {#activity2}

**Time**: 25 minutes

**Goal**: Run a statistical test and interpret the results

Choose ONE of these three hypotheses to test:

## Option A: Mood Change (Paired t-test)

**Hypothesis**: Mood changed from before to after the session

```{webr-r}
# Option A: Paired t-test
# Did mood change?

# Step 1: Visualise the change
mood_change <- merged |>
  select(participant_id, mood_pre_1, mood_post_1) |>
  mutate(change = mood_post_1 - mood_pre_1)

ggplot(mood_change, aes(x = change)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#27ae60", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Mood Change (Post - Pre)", y = "Count",
       title = "Did Mood Change?")
```

```{webr-r}
# Step 2: Run the paired t-test
t.test(merged$mood_post_1, merged$mood_pre_1, paired = TRUE)
```

```{webr-r}
# Step 3: Calculate effect size
diff <- merged$mood_post_1 - merged$mood_pre_1
cohens_d <- mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE) / sd(diff, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d, 2))
cat("\n\nInterpretation: 0.2 = small, 0.5 = medium, 0.8 = large")
```

## Option B: Word Type Effect (Independent t-test)

**Hypothesis**: Concrete words (Lab B) are easier to remember than abstract words (Lab A)

```{webr-r}
# Option B: Independent samples t-test
# Are concrete words easier to remember than abstract words?

# Step 1: Visualise by group
merged |>
  filter(!is.na(mem_total_1) & !is.na(lab_room)) |>
  mutate(lab = factor(lab_room, labels = c("Lab A\n(Abstract)", "Lab B\n(Concrete)"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = lab, y = mem_total_1, fill = lab)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#3498db", "#e67e22")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Words Recalled",
       title = "Memory: Abstract vs Concrete Words") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{webr-r}
# Step 2: Run independent t-test
lab_a <- merged |> filter(lab_room == 1) |> pull(mem_total_1)  # Abstract
lab_b <- merged |> filter(lab_room == 2) |> pull(mem_total_1)  # Concrete

t.test(lab_a, lab_b)
```

```{webr-r}
# Step 3: Calculate effect size
lab_a <- lab_a[!is.na(lab_a)]
lab_b <- lab_b[!is.na(lab_b)]
pooled_sd <- sqrt((var(lab_a) + var(lab_b)) / 2)
cohens_d <- (mean(lab_b) - mean(lab_a)) / pooled_sd  # Concrete - Abstract
cat("Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d, 2))
```

## Option C: Sixth Sense (One-sample t-test)

**Hypothesis**: Detection accuracy was better than chance (50%)

```{webr-r}
# Option C: One-sample t-test
# Was sixth sense accuracy better than chance?

# Step 1: Visualise distribution
ggplot(merged, aes(x = stare_accuracy)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, fill = "#9b59b6", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Accuracy", y = "Count",
       title = "Sixth Sense Accuracy",
       subtitle = "Red line = chance (50%)")
```

```{webr-r}
# Step 2: Run one-sample t-test against 0.5
t.test(merged$stare_accuracy, mu = 0.5)
```

```{webr-r}
# Step 3: Calculate effect size
cohens_d <- (mean(merged$stare_accuracy) - 0.5) / sd(merged$stare_accuracy)
cat("Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d, 2))
```

# Activity 3: Explore a Relationship {#activity3}

**Time**: 25 minutes

**Goal**: Create a scatterplot and calculate a correlation

Choose ONE relationship to explore:

## Option A: Self-Rating vs Performance (Calibration)

Are people accurate judges of their own ability?

```{webr-r}
# Option A: Self-rating vs throwing accuracy
merged <- merged |>
  mutate(throw_accuracy = throw_dom_success / 10 * 100)

ggplot(merged, aes(x = throw_self_rating_1, y = throw_accuracy)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#3498db") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#e74c3c") +
  labs(
    x = "Self-Rating (1-10)",
    y = "Actual Accuracy (%)",
    title = "Are You Calibrated?",
    subtitle = "Self-perception vs reality"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

```{webr-r}
# Correlation test
cor.test(merged$throw_self_rating_1, merged$throw_accuracy)
```

## Option B: Extraversion vs Mood Change

Do extraverts enjoy the session more?

```{webr-r}
# Option B: Extraversion vs mood change
merged <- merged |>
  mutate(mood_change = mood_post_1 - mood_pre_1)

ggplot(merged, aes(x = tipi_1, y = mood_change)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#27ae60") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#e74c3c") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Extraversion Score",
    y = "Mood Change (Post - Pre)",
    title = "Does Personality Predict Enjoyment?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

```{webr-r}
cor.test(merged$tipi_1, merged$mood_change)
```

## Option C: Sleep and Reaction Time

Does sleep affect performance?

```{webr-r}
# Option C: Create your own exploration!
# Example: Stress and memory
ggplot(merged, aes(x = stress_pre_1, y = mem_total_1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#e74c3c") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#3498db") +
  labs(
    x = "Pre-Session Stress",
    y = "Words Recalled",
    title = "Does Stress Affect Memory?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

```{webr-r}
cor.test(merged$stress_pre_1, merged$mem_total_1)
```

## Interpreting Correlations

| r value | Strength |
|---------|----------|
| 0.1 - 0.3 | Weak |
| 0.3 - 0.5 | Moderate |
| 0.5 - 0.7 | Strong |
| > 0.7 | Very strong |
